text:
Marta: heads up — did the AWQ (4-bit) bakeoff on the new 7B variant for the summarization + QA suites. results look bad: Rouge-L down ~6.7 points on news-sum, QA EM down 9.4 points on squad-like, and hallucination rate jumped from ~2% to ~18% on our hallucination probe. :warning: sample and logs below.

Sam: yikes. did you run the same prompt templates & normalization? could this be detokenization/formatting? :eyes:

Marta: same eval harness, seed, and prompts. I reran canonical normalization step (strip trailing spaces, unify quotes) and numbers persist. AB test config: AWQ-4 (default group=64, blockwise per 128), compared to baseline FP16 and GPTQ-8.

Lee: can you paste the eval summary (numbers)? also any examples of hallucinations?

Marta: sure — pasted from Eval report below:

EvalBot: 
```
Bench, Baseline(FP16), AWQ-4, Delta
news-sum Rouge-L, 42.1, 35.4, -6.7
squad-like QA EM, 78.6, 69.2, -9.4
format-preserve (json format tests) exact-match, 96.5, 89.1, -7.4
halluc-probe (rate), 2.1%, 18.3%, +16.2pp
```

And a concrete hallucination sample (from news-sum):

Marta: "Input: 'Company X announced acquisition of Y last quarter.'
Baseline: 'Company X acquired Y in Q3 to expand retail presence.'
AWQ-4: 'Company X sold its entire cloud division to Z for $2.3B and laid off 1,200 people.'"

Priya: that's pretty bad, AWQ blew up factuality. could be quantization noise in key layers (attn output or lm head). did you run per-layer error diagnostics?

Marta: ran layer-wise KL and SNR quick checks — biggest shifts in layers 22-26 (mid-to-late), and logit variance increased notably at generation steps 3-7. I can share plots if useful.

Anand: possible causes: group size mismatch, per-channel vs per-tensor scale, or failing outlier handling. AWQ often compresses outliers aggressively; GPTQ with outlier handling sometimes better for fidelity. Have we tried GPTQ/AWQ hypervariants?

Marta: compared AWQ default vs GPTQ-8 and INT8-LLM. GPTQ-8 drop was smaller: Rouge-L -2.1, QA -3.0, hallucination +4.8pp. INT8-LLM (symmetric per-channel) was in-between. FP8 emulation (experimental) actually matched FP16 on some samples but is unstable across seeds.

Lee: important to know deployment profile: this is for Dedicated low-latency path (batch=1, kv-cache warm). AWQ artifacts used for the Dedicated pool could cause customer regressions if rolled out. We should block rollout on this model for now.

Sam: agree — block rollout. also add targeted evals: (1) hallucination probe at 5k queries, (2) per-task formatting test (json outputs), (3) beam vs greedy checks. can we get quantization config used?

InfraBot: AWQ run artifact: s3://redwood-artifacts/quant/7b/awq/1752003456/ ; command: 
```
awq_convert --model /artifacts/7b/fp16/model.pt --bits 4 --group-size 64 --out s3://... --per-channel True
```
Logs: s3://redwood-logs/quant/1752003456.log
```

Priya: next steps I propose:
- reproduce locally with group-size 32/128 and per-channel=False/True to see sensitivity
- run layer-by-layer dequant check (swap FP16 for suspect layers 22-26 into quantized model) to isolate culprit
- run GPTQ with group=128 + outlier handling on top of same checkpoint
- run high-sample hallucination probe (10k) and store token-level traces for forensic analysis

Marta: I'm on repro. starting runs now with group-size [32,128], and GPTQ-8 baseline. tagging @Sam to block the rollout job.

Sam: blocked the rollout pipeline for artifact 1752003456 and opened incident ticket INF-5982. Adding regression gate to prevent any auto-promote from quant pipelines until we close the investigation. :thumbsup:

Lee: also add a formatting normalization step before eval (we saw json formatting EM drop). maybe quantization increases off-by-one tokens or special token mapping issues.

Anand: if layer-swap isolates it, we can either skip quantizing those layers or increase precision there (mixed-precision: 8-bit for output-proj / lm-head). AWQ supports per-layer override in latest.

Marta: good plan. will paste quick diffs and a few more example failures once repro finishes (~30m). thanks team. :coffee:
